## crystal tarot and the basic RWS
i picked the crystal tarot for its vibrant green, it feels springy. the RWS was simply one of the leftover decks that didn't get its own definite month, so i paired it up with the crystal as a "safe" bet, seeing as the crystal tarot uses the picard system which i'm not all that comfortable with.
well, my "safe bet" deck immediately went back on the shelf. while i can read it easily, the art is just extremely off-putting, i just never feel like reaching for it. the crystal tarot is much more attractive and appealing to look at, but doesn't speak too clearly. and to be fair, i have no real interest in learning the picard system. i'm trying to read "despite" it, not integrating it.

# march decks

## ritual tarot and the thoth
i picked both of these for their "Pow!" aries sort of feeling, to welcome in the spring and the new astrological year. but it quickly turned out i see them more as magical tools than just plain old tarot decks. the effect was twofold:
1. i followed a rabbit hole of thoth creators that pointed me back towards mysticism, which resulted in a renewed, inspired spiritual practice
2. when i wanted to just fool around with some cards, i reached instead for regular old playing cards, so that was quite fun.
in effect, the month itself wasn't all that much about tarot. as for my deck impressions - both of these are "good" decks. i used the ritual tarot a bit for introspective readings and what Esther from mindful tarot calls "wobble readings". i love the imagery, there's something primal and universal about it. using images of ancient art and artifacts together with landscape photography makes the art feel like it taps into a broad current of humanity. there's a sense of belonging and togetherness, both with other people and with the earth itself. at the same time the predominant colors seem to be blue and black, which to me grants it a bit of

While I agree that the web stuff is getting ridiculous, it's factually incorrect to say "CSS was invented to fix HTML", and JS was invented to fix HTML/CSS. CSS wasn't invented to "fix" HTML, it was invented to style HTML separately so that you could apply different styles to the same page. And JS was invented to make pages more dynamic. Has nothing to do with "fixing" HTML or CSS.

It seems the article is being very anachronistic in saying this; they see problems with HTML, therefore CSS *must have* been invented to "fix" HTML. In reality, the problems that the article's writer might see with HTML are not the same problems that people saw during the time CSS was invented.

I tend to be along the anti-web-technologies side for most things; I don't want HTML and CSS crap in all my applications.

Questions which seemingly cannot be raised without touching off holy wars, such as 

> What is the best operating system (or editor, language, architecture, shell, mail reader, news reader)?

,

# No-cost theological and biblical studies resources

Many neurodivergent people find the topics of theology, biblical studies, studies of religions, philosophy, and ethics interesting, even if they do not necessarily believe in them uncritically. At the same time, they often find conventional schooling extremely challenging. 

Here I have made a list of no-cost resources that offer college-level lectures and courses. They can be accessed from anywhere with access to the Internet.  

Please note that most of these institutions are very conservative theologically and politically, as they tend to be the ones who are more willing to offer free educational opportunities that they believe would advance their missions and objectives. Nevertheless, even within such institutions, professors and academics are less likely to be doctrinaire conservatives or fundamentalists, and you will find many of their offerings quite valuable for your education. Theology is the study of religious belief from a religious perspective, with a focus on the nature of divinity and the history behind religion. It is taught as an academic discipline, typically in universities and seminaries. It occupies itself with the unique content of analyzing the supernatural, but also deals with religious epistemology; moreover, it asks and seeks to answer the question of revelation, which pertains to the acceptance of deities, as not only transcendent or above the natural world, but also willing and able to interact with the natural world and to reveal themselves to humankind. 

Theologians use various forms of analysis and argument (experiential, philosophical, ethnographic, historical, and others) to help understand, explain, test, critique, defend or promote any myriad of religious topics. => /u/LucasMW In: u/LucasMW

While I agree that the web stuff is getting ridiculous, it's factually incorrect to say "CSS was invented to fix HTML", and JS was invented to fix HTML/CSS. CSS wasn't invented to "fix" HTML, it was invented to style HTML separately so that you could apply different styles to the same page. And JS was invented to make pages more dynamic. Has nothing to do with "fixing" HTML or CSS.

It seems the article is being very anachronistic in saying this; they see problems with HTML, therefore CSS *must have* been invented to "fix" HTML. In reality, the problems that the article's writer might see with HTML are not the same problems that people saw during the time CSS was invented.

I tend to be along the anti-web-technologies side for most things; I don't want HTML and CSS crap in all my applications. I don't want Electron stupidity. # Day 11
~4 days left
Saturday, August 28th, 2021AD

## Way Monastery museums

Day 1 of 2 at the Way monastery was restful for the most part. We got up and had a nice breakfast and managed to get to the very end of Liturgy this morning. Afterward, we visited the museums within the monastery grounds. One was about the local ruler, now canonized as a saint, and how he defended the country and built monasteries for each of his military victories against the Turks. The other museum was commemorating the 150th anniversary of the idea of a unified country, as well as a huge congress on unity that took place at the monastery in the 1800s. I liked the local ruler’s museum, which had a lot of interesting burial shrouds and manuscripts written with still-legible Cyrillic text. Nia gvidanto interrupted and spoke for me only twice, although one of those times was when I was reading some text from a shroud and the monk showing us around asked if I could read Slavonic.

We packed up our stuff and left the little monastery in the mountains. We drove north, stopping at a monastery renowned for its blue frescos. # Scott Pilgrim vs. the World (Movie)

4 of 5 Stars

Scott Pilgrim vs. the World is a fun, funny mash-up of movie, comic book and video game sensibilities. The story combines a romantic comedy with a fighting video game, and the film just runs full-tilt with the idea.

Every new relationship comes with baggage. In this case, the baggage happens to be Ramona Flowers' seven evil exes, who all want to fight Scott Pilgrim if he's going to date her. Fights are staged like video games, with “X vs Y” captions, physics-defying moves and special powers, and defeated opponents transforming into coins. Caption boxes provide extra information. Flashbacks are illustrated in comic-strip form.

Its biggest flaw, IMO, is that it tries so hard to fit all the battles into one movie that it forgets to slow down and show us that Scott and Ramona actually like each other (most of the time). There's no real sense of time, and it feels like the whole thing could happen in a week. # Scott Pilgrim Takes Off

5 of 5 Stars

Scott Pilgrim Takes Off is a weird cartoon. In a lot of good ways.

It's sort of a combination of the movie and the original comics, combining the art style (now animated!) with the movie's voice cast and a longer run time (eight episodes on Netflix) that makes it possible to actually dig into the characters and story. It's sort of a reunion show, sort of a remake, and sort of a "What If..."

=> ../movies/scott-pilgrim.gmi the movie

Because at the end of the anime's* first episode it, well, takes off into a totally new direction, telling a new story focusing this time on Ramona Flowers and her relationships with her various "evil exes," reacting to, bouncing off of and critiquing the comics and movie. (Several characters actually start filming the movie during the show...which goes off the rails in yet another direction.)

The craziness is dialed up to 11, with video game, comic book and anime tropes used to reexamine who these characters are. Scott could easily have become the next Evil Ex, and he had a tendency to rewrite his own backstory to make him look better. And Ramona wasn't entirely blameless in her past relationships

# Cults Utilizing the Gemini Occult Meaning

The **Gemini occult meaning** is tied to symbolism around **duality, twins, and the spiritual duality of mortal personality vs. immortal spirit**, inspired by the myth of Castor and Pollux. Many esoteric traditions and cults use Gemini symbolism to represent spiritual ideas, prophecy, or mystery.

## Cults and Traditions Utilizing Gemini Occult Meaning

=> gemini://rhun-cult.example Rhun's Cult (Tolkien-inspired)
A cult linked to Tolkien's lore uses the Gemini constellation symbolically in prophecy involving twin leaders. Here, the twins represent duality and leadership themes.

=> gemini://mithraism.example Mithraism (Roman Mystery Cult)
Though centered on Mithras and the bull, this mystery religion includes astral symbolism with zodiacal connections. Gemini’s themes of duality connect indirectly with their cosmic cycles.

=> gemini://christian-esoterism.example Christian Mystical Interpretation ("Gospel in the Stars")
Certain Christian esoteric views see Gemini as symbolic of Christ and the Church—divine twins signifying spiritual union and dual divine roles.
